narrative.overview:
AutoAnsys dresses CFD work in a race team's graphic system. The ground is technical white (#F7F7F4), the ink is near-black (#14161B), and exactly one committed color field exists in the chrome: the racing-blue nav rail. Every run is a numbered, striped entry in the team's season — a deterministic three-band livery stripe and a two-digit roundel car number derived from its id — so one design iteration is recognizable at a glance across lists, charts, and comparisons. The world explicitly refuses the category default: no graphite dashboard, no single teal accent, no shadowed cards.

Density is real-data density: tables and stat strips set in JetBrains Mono tabular numerals, condensed-caps labels, hairline seams instead of elevation. Color is disciplined — state hues (green/amber/red) carry meaning only, the six-hue livery palette carries identity only, and chrome stays ink on ground. Terminal states are declared, not hidden: a run that fails gets an angled rubber stamp, not a quiet gray badge.
keyCharacteristics: One committed color field (the racing-blue rail); the rest of the chrome is ink on white
Deterministic run identity: livery stripe + roundel number, consistent across every surface
Hairline seams, zero drop shadows; depth by border weight and tone
JetBrains Mono tabular numerals for every data number
Data graphics live inside bordered "Fig." plates with captions
Stamped terminal verdicts (Finished / Failed / Cancelled) at -6°
One authored entrance animation (`settle`), route-level only

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: Racing blue is the only large color field in the chrome, and it belongs to the nav rail. Everywhere else, blue appears only as small committed accents (primary button, focus, active tab).

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: Color for data (charts, contours, series hues) lives inside bordered plates with "Fig." captions. Chrome stays ink on ground.

rules.name: The Identity-Is-Not-State Rule
rules.body: Livery hues identify runs; state hues judge them. The two palettes share #1d43d8 and #d92d20 by value but never swap roles.

rules.name: The Mono Numerals Rule
rules.body: Any number a user might compare or scan down a column is set in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures. Archivo never carries data numerals.

rules.name: The Condensed Caps Rule
rules.body: Labels, buttons, and section heads are Saira Condensed 700 uppercase with wide tracking (0.08–0.16em). Archivo stays sentence-case.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: Panels never float. If two regions need separating, draw a 1px seam; if a moment needs weight, thicken the rule to 2px ink — never add a shadow.

rules.name: The One Entrance Rule
rules.body: .settle fires once per route or dialog mount, never scattered per-card.

dos: Do give every run-shaped entity its Stripe + Roundel from lib/livery.ts; identity must survive across lists, charts, and compare.
Do set every comparable numeral in JetBrains Mono with .tnum.
Do put any chart, contour, or color-bearing data graphic inside a Plate with a "Fig." caption.
Do stamp terminal states on detail headers (Finished / Failed / Cancelled) and keep the failure's error_message readable beside it.
Do isolate Cancel/Delete with surrounding space and the two-step ConfirmButton.
Do keep labels in Saira Condensed 700 uppercase with 0.08–0.16em tracking, and section heads trailing their hairline to the edge.
donts: Don't add drop shadows; separation is seams (1px #dcdcd4) or heavy ink rules (2px), never elevation.
Don't introduce a second large color field; racing blue's field is the rail, full stop.
Don't use livery hues for state or state hues for decoration; green, amber, and red appear only where they judge something.
Don't round beyond 3px on controls (4px on the stamp); panels and plates stay square.
Don't scatter entrance animations per card; .settle is route/dialog level only, and all motion collapses under prefers-reduced-motion.
Don't fall back to the category default — graphite dashboard, teal accent, shadowed cards — anywhere in this product.
